senses.gloss: to be narrow, slender, young, v. צוֹעֵר, צׇעִיר.

units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6:4">Gen. R. s. 6</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="R00661"><he>הצעיר</he></cite>, <cite ref="Genesis 48:14">Gen. XLVIII, 14</cite>) <he>על ידי שהיה מַצְעִיר את עסקיו וכ׳</he> because he subordinated his affairs (was contented with lesser services), he was privileged to be invested with the rights of the firstborn; <he>הגדול שהוא מצעיר וכ׳</he> if a great man applies himself to minor services, how much more (is he praiseworthy)!—Part. pass. <cite ref="M00577"><he>מוּצְעָר</he></cite>, q. v.

senses.gloss: to narrow, restrain; to inflict pain, annoy.
units: <cite ref="Nazir 19a:5">Naz. 19ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Nazir 22a:4">22ᵃ</cite>, a. e. (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 6:11">Num. VI, 11</cite>) <he>ומה זה שלא צי׳ עצמו … המְצַעֵר עצמו וכ׳</he> if this (Nazarite) who denied himself only the enjoyment of wine is called a sinner, how much more so he who denies himself all enjoyments of life! <cite ref="Taanit 11a:8">Taan. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>יִצְעַר … במשה רבינו שצי׳ עצמו וכ׳</he> man must suffer (deny himself enjoyments), when the community suffers; for thus we find that Moses afflicted himself (by sitting on a stone, <cite ref="Exodus 17:12">Ex. XVII, 12</cite>) &c.; <cite ref="Exodus 17:12">ib.</cite> <he>וכל המצער עצמו עם וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>וכל המצער עם</he>, insert <he>עצמו</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) and he who afflicts himself in sympathy with the community, will be allowed to see the comfort of the community; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 148:7">Yalk. Gen. 148</cite>, a. e. <cite ref="R00661"><he>המִצְטַעֵר</he></cite>.

Snh. 11ᵃ אתה הוא שצִיעַרְתָּ לאבא wast thou the one who annoyed my father (with the smell of garlic)? Ab. Zar. 40ᵇ ואתה מְצַעֲרֵינִי and thou didst let me be in pain (without telling me of the remedy)?; a. fr.—2) *to suffer.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 333">Yalk. Is. 333</cite>, v. <cite ref="R00735"><he>צָרַר</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to feel pain; to suffer privation; to grieve, trouble one’s self. Yalk. Gen. l. c., a. e., v. supra.
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 15b:11">Ḥag. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>בזמן שאדם מִצְטַעֵר וכ׳</he> when a man suffers (the penalty of the law), what does the Shekhinah say?; <he>אם כך הקב״ה מצטער וכ׳</he> if the Lord thus grieves over the blood of the wicked (convict), how much more does he grieve over the blood of the righteous that is shed!; Ms. M. 1 <he>אם כן מצטער אני וכ׳</he>; Ms. M. 2 <he>מִצְטַעֲרֵנִי</he> if thus I (the Lord) grieve &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 46a">Snh. 46ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 930">Yalk. Deut. 930</cite>.
<cite ref="Sukkah 26a">Succ. 26ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מצטער פטור וכ׳</he> he that feels uncomfortable (cold) is exempt from sitting in the Succah (contrad. fr. <cite ref="H00333"><he>חולה</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Megillah 16a">Meg. 16ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>אפשר דבר שנצ׳ בו … יכשל בו</he> is it possible that this righteous man (Joseph) should commit the same wrong from which he himself had suffered (to make distinctions between brothers)? <cite ref="Yoma 74b">Yoma 74ᵇ</cite>; Y. ib. VIII, 44ᵈ top (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 16:29">Lev. XVI, 29</cite>) <he>יכול ישב … ויִצְטַעֵר</he> you may think, one must sit in the sun or in the cold in order to afflict one’s self. Bab. ib. 19ᵇ <he>כל ימי הייתי מצט׳ על וכ׳</he> all my life-time have I been troubling myself about this verse (<cite ref="Leviticus 16:2">Lev. XVI, 2</cite>) thinking, when shall I have an opportunity to carry it into practice (in accordance with the Sadducean interpretation of it) &c.
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 354:5">Sifré Deut. 354</cite> <he>הואיל ונִצְטַעַרְנוּ וכ׳</he> since we have gone to the trouble of coming here &c.; a. fr.
